think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 35-year-old man presents with acute right scrotal pain, swelling, fever, and leukocytosis 2 years after bowel resection for a strangulated inguinal hernia, complicated by live nematode worms extruding through a cutaneous sinus at the root of the scrotum. The clinical syndrome strongly mimics acute bacterial epididymo-orchitis, scrotal abscess, or recurrent incarcerated hernia with enterocutaneous fistula; the critical challenge is identifying an aberrant extra-intestinal migration of a soil-transmitted helminth traversing the previous surgical tract into the tunica vaginalis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation narrative encompasses the patient's acute 2-day history of right scrotal pain, fever, prior surgical history (inguinoscrotal incision for strangulated hernia), physical findings of local erythema, warmth, tenderness, tachycardia, fever, leukocytosis, and gross observation of cylindrical parasitic worms (4-12 cm long with curved posterior ends) extruding from the scrotal base. The breakpoint ends prior to surgical exploration of the tunica vaginalis sac, post-operative albendazole administration, and definitive parasitologic identification of Ascaris lumbricoides.
3. Differential Distinctions: Acute bacterial epididymo-orchitis or testicular torsion typically presents with acute unilateral scrotal pain, fever, and leukocytosis, but lacks external fistula formation or macroscopic worm extrusion, and surgical exploration in this case demonstrated a completely normal testis. Recurrent strangulated inguinal hernia with perforation was considered given his surgical history, but ruled out operatively by the absence of herniated intestinal loops, necrosis, or purulent peritonitis, revealing instead clear hydrocele fluid within the tunica vaginalis harboring live nematodes.
case_prompt:
A 35-year-old man presents with sudden-onset severe pain over the right side of his scrotum and fever of 2 days' duration. Earlier on the day of presentation, he noticed macroscopic cylindrical worms extruding through a cutaneous opening at the root of the scrotum. His surgical history is notable for an emergency repair of a right-sided strangulated inguinal hernia 2 years prior, which required bowel resection and anastomosis performed through an inguinoscrotal incision.

On physical examination, the patient appears anxious, febrile, and tachycardic. Genitourinary examination reveals significant swelling, erythema, and shiny taut skin over the right hemiscrotum, with marked local warmth and exquisite tenderness to palpation. Several live, cylindrical nematodes measuring 4 to 12 cm in length, some exhibiting ventrally curved posterior ends, are actively emerging from the root of the right scrotum. The left hemiscrotum and left testis are entirely normal. Initial triage laboratory testing demonstrates marked peripheral leukocytosis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute unilateral scrotal erythema, severe tenderness, high fever, and leukocytosis, but excluded by the macroscopic extrusion of live nematodes and intraoperative demonstration of a healthy, uninvolved testis and clear hydrocele fluid.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Right side of scrotum was swollen, red and overlying skin was shiny. Local temperature was raised and it was tender to touch. Left scrotum was normal... Hydrocele fluid was clear. Testis was normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Recurrent Strangulated Inguinal Hernia with Enterocutaneous Fistula
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to previous surgery for strangulated hernia and bowel resection, but ruled out because scrotal exploration showed no herniated visceral contents, peritoneal defect, or purulent enterocutaneous fistula.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He had undergone surgery for right-sided strangulated inguinal hernia 2 years back. Resection and anastomosis was done through inguino scrotal incision... Right side of scrotum was explored and all the worms present in the tunica vaginalis sac (containing hydrocele fluid) were taken out.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The pivotal clinical and operative confirmation was established by emergency right scrotal exploration revealing adult cylindrical nematodes inhabiting the tunica vaginalis sac alongside clear hydrocele fluid, confirming ectopic scrotal ascariasis through a pre-existing patent surgical pathway.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Local examination revealed adult Ascaris worms (4-12 cm long, some with ventrally curved tail end) coming out of the root of scrotum [Figure 1]... Right side of scrotum was explored and all the worms present in the tunica vaginalis sac (containing hydrocele fluid) were taken out.

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint placed immediately prior to surgical exploration. Pathogen name ('Ascaris') strictly removed from case_prompt while preserving physical description (4-12 cm worms with curved tails). Differential clearly contrasts acute epididymo-orchitis and strangulated hernia recurrence.
